name: Neglect of Probability
description: When an outcome is vivid or emotionally charged, people can react to the possibility itself while underweighting how likely it actually is. A 1% chance and a 99% chance can evoke surprisingly similar concern if the imagined outcome is intense enough.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to safety, privacy, moderation, security, and health UX: both teams and users can anchor on a vivid worst-case scenario while failing to calibrate their reaction to its real likelihood.
prevalence_note: Known in risk communication, safety, and policy-adjacent design, but usually implicit rather than explicitly named in ordinary UX critique.

findings.description: Across five risky-choice studies, willingness to pay to avoid affect-rich outcomes varied much less with probability than willingness to pay for affect-poor monetary outcomes, indicating that vivid affect can swamp sensitivity to likelihood.
findings.source_title: Money, Kisses, and Electric Shocks: On the Affective Psychology of Risk

findings.description: Reported to argue and demonstrate, via experiments (electric-shock, arsenic-exposure scenarios) and real regulatory/public-response case studies (hazardous-waste-site fear, the Alar pesticide panic, post-9/11 anthrax response), that emotionally vivid worst-case outcomes cause people and institutions to neglect the actual probability of occurrence -- the original coining and case-based demonstration of probability neglect, independent of and predating the corpus's existing Rottenstreich & Hsee (2001) lab-based affect-rich-gamble evidence. This description is drawn from the paper's well-established secondary characterization and this entry's own prior review note, not independently verified against the primary text this session.
findings.source_title: Probability Neglect: Emotions, Worst Cases, and Law
